job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

passage: Creating a secure digital identity requires careful habits. First, always use a strong, unique password that does not include personal details like your pet’s name or your birthday, as these are easy for others to guess. A password like 'Ravi@1' is weak because it is short and predictable, even with a symbol. Second, never share your One-Time Password (OTP) with anyone, regardless of who they claim to be or if they know your name. Banks and legitimate companies will never ask you to disclose an OTP over a phone call or message. Third, remember that privacy settings on social media are not absolute; once you post content, it can still be screenshotted or shared by others, even if your profile is private. Finally, be aware that cyberbullying is a serious issue that causes real emotional harm, even without physical contact. If you experience harassment, do not respond with anger or handle it alone; instead, report the behavior to a trusted adult or the platform authorities immediately. By following these steps, you protect your data and maintain a safe online environment for yourself and your peers.

items.evidence: A password like 'Ravi@1' is weak because it is short and predictable, even with a symbol.
items.q: Meena's password is 'Tom@7'. It has a capital letter, a symbol and a number. Why is it still weak?
options: It is short and easy to guess
It has no letters changed into numbers
It needs more capitals and numbers in it
It is used for only one account
items.explain: Like 'Ravi@1', it is short and predictable, so a symbol or number does not make it strong.

wrong.why: thinks swapping letters for numbers makes a password strong
thinks adding capitals and numbers is enough, even if the password is short
thinks using one password for every account is better

items.evidence: First, always use a strong, unique password that does not include personal details like your pet’s name or your birthday, as these are easy for others to guess.
items.q: Kabir makes his password from his dog's name and his date of birth. Is this a safe password?
options: No, people who know him could guess it
Yes, only Kabir knows these personal details
Yes, if he changes letters into numbers
No, until he adds a capital and a number
items.explain: A pet's name and birthday are personal details that others can easily guess, so the password is not safe.

wrong.why: thinks personal details are secret because only they know them
thinks number swaps fix a guessable password
thinks one capital and one number make any password safe

items.evidence: Second, never share your One-Time Password (OTP) with anyone, regardless of who they claim to be or if they know your name.
items.q: A caller says he is from Asha's bank, knows her full name, and asks for her OTP. What should she do?
options: Refuse, as nobody should ever receive her OTP
Share it, since he already knows her name
Share it, so her account does not get blocked
Refuse, unless the OTP is only four digits
items.explain: Never share an OTP with anyone, whoever they say they are and even if they know your name.

wrong.why: trusts a caller who knows their name
fears the account will be blocked without the OTP
thinks only long OTPs are dangerous to share

items.evidence: Third, remember that privacy settings on social media are not absolute; once you post content, it can still be screenshotted or shared by others, even if your profile is private.
items.q: Neha's profile is private, so only her friends can see her photo. Could the photo still spread to others?
options: Yes, a friend could screenshot and share it
No, a private profile stops all sharing
No, she can delete it and it is gone
Yes, but only once her profile is public
items.explain: Privacy settings are not absolute; once posted, others can screenshot or share content even from a private profile.

wrong.why: thinks a private profile means nothing can be shared
thinks deleting a post removes it forever
misses 'even if your profile is private' in the passage
